home.subtitle: OpenSource Rolemaster assistant for create campaigns, manage factions, resolve tactical combats and keep your sessions organized with a clean, extendable toolset.
home.module-core-desc: Adjust game settings such as the creation of realms, races and professions, and define the general game configuration. You can use the standard RMU settings or create as many game-specific customisations as you like.
home.module-strategic-desc: Create a game with your friends using characters from a specific realm. The strategic mode allows you to create characters, equip them, and set the rules for the campaign you’ll be playing. Create your own factions and customise the characters who will be involved in future matches.
home.module-tactical-desc: Once you’ve created a campaign in tactical mode, you can battle against other players or the environment. Simply choose who’s taking part in the battle and roll the dice.
home.module-npcs-desc: Use the game's NPCs or create your own. NPCs can range from a level-one sheep to a specific level-500 character. Good luck with it.
home.module-spells-desc: Use the spells from the game's default spell lists or create your own spell lists.

about-intro-1: I’m someone who discovered Rolemaster and MERP in the early 90s and, after many years without playing, a bit of a midlife crisis has brought me back to this beloved game.
about-intro-2: Now, 25 years on from those games I used to play with my brother, we’ve got together again to move around Lord of the Rings miniatures, eat pizza and roll the dice.
about-app-text-1: In 2021, I started developing an app for playing <link>RMSS</link> for my own use, as a tool to streamline games. When the app was already quite far along, one afternoon whilst looking at my phone I discovered that a new version of Rolemaster was about to be released.
about-app-text-2: So I thought: it’s a bit of a cheek that, after two decades without any new content, they’ve had to release a version right now, just when I’d almost got all the features I wanted!!!
about-app-text-3: Then, during the 2025 holidays, I said to myself, Right, let’s start again, this time by creating a helper tool for the new system.
about-app-image-text: With all this programming, I haven't had time to paint lately!
about-before-text-1: When I was very young, I started using spreadsheets to speed up games and create characters, because whilst doing it with pen and paper has its charm, it ends up being very time-consuming.
about-before-text-2: So, without any knowledge of programming, I began automating certain tasks, mainly the damage tables, so I wouldn’t have to keep looking up the row and column for the Arms Law of the time And those were my first steps in programming, a profession I’ve been working in for 20 years.
about-now-text-1: Now, after many years without playing and having passed my forties, I wanted to recapture those afternoons spent rolling open-ended dices and feel once more what it’s like when a level-one goblin has to roll the dice on the critical hit table.
about-now-text-2: Many of the adventures I prepared back then, with extensive maps and plenty of storytelling, ended with the main character sadly bleeding to death in the mud of a meadow after an encounter on the encounter table with a wild boar and her piglets.
about-now-text-3: That was one of the things I liked most about Rolemaster, its system suited less epic scenarios far better than other 80s role-playing games.
about-motivation-text-1: Although I used to play narrative campaigns as a child, the main focus of these was the combat, where you’d end up using miniatures as if it were a small-scale wargame. I’ve always enjoyed these games and have played quite a few of them, mainly 40k.
about-motivation-text-2: I liked gang management games in the style of Necromunda, where you had a small group of characters and simply faced off against another gang.
about-motivation-text-3: And I thought, this style of play, set in Middle-earth – which is by far the setting I’ve always liked best – using Rolemaster rules could work quite well.
about-motivation-image-text: Amon Sûl surrounded by buildings? What happened?
about-testing-text-1: After a few months of development, I finally enlisted my brother to test whether the project was actually feasible, or whether running a game with so many characters and rules would prove too complicated.
about-testing-text-2: The idea was to use a tablet next to the table to work out movements, attacks, manoeuvres… whilst rolling the dice and taking measurements, checking the lines of sight on the table to see what cover an archer’s target would have…
about-testing-text-3: And after several games, I’m happy with the result and I think it’s possible to combine the world of miniature skirmishes with the depth of rules that Rolemaster brings

docs-intro: This section covers the first steps for using the tool, creating a campaign, developing characters and setting up a game.
docs-official-content-text: First of all, you’ll need the <link>official ICE content</link> to play! This tool is a guide that doesn’t cover the entire game. It simply helps to streamline certain actions, such as character management and combat management.
docs-rulebooks-text: To use this assistant you should own the official rulebooks. These are available on DriveThruRPG, where you can find the full rules and game content. This assistant does not cover every option in the rules; it is intended as a practical tool to help manage characters and sessions.
docs-approach-text: Assuming familiarity with Rolemaster concepts, the application focuses on the following core ideas:
docs-concept-realm: Realms: A realm defines the fictional universe for a campaign. This could be, for example, Shadow World, the official ICE universe, a realistic medieval setting without magic or Tolkien’s Middle-earth
docs-concept-strategic-game: Strategic game: Equivalent to a campaign. It contains factions, groups, and the collection of characters and resources that make up a long-running campaign.
docs-concept-faction: Faction: A faction is a group of characters tied to a campaign. It can also represent a set of NPCs (for example, the goblins guarding a dungeon).
docs-concept-character: Character: A player character built using RMU design rules — attributes, skills, items and other customisations.
docs-concept-npc: NPC: A non-player actor created either manually or derived from module content. NPCs are assigned levels, skills, equipment and hit points directly rather than through character construction rules.
docs-concept-tactical-game: Tactical game: Encounters and sessions that generally involve actions and combat, played with a board and miniatures. From the tactical dashboard you declare and resolve maneuvers, movement, combat, resistance rolls and other actions.
docs-creating-game-text-1: First, you must choose a Realm. You can use the default realms available in the app or create a new one. Creating a realm takes some time, as it involves setting up each of the races and customisations for that realm.
docs-creating-game-text-2: Once inside the realm, you will create a ‘Strategic game’. Within the game, we’ll select certain features such as the experience multiplier and the board scale (which we’ll use to adapt the distances calculated by the app to our scale for playing with miniatures. For example, for 28mm miniatures, we can choose a scale of 0.5 to play in inches on a standard wargame board).

technical-intro: This section explains the technical structure of the project for running it locally
technical-prerequisites: This guide assumes you have a basic understanding of Docker, Git, Node.js and TypeScript. If you don’t, setting up the application may prove a little tricky
technical-architecture: The application is built using a microservices and micro-frontend (MFE) architecture. APIs are built using <nestjs>NestJS</nestjs> following a CQRS pattern. The front-end uses <react>React</react> and <mui>MUI</mui> for its UI components.
technical-external-tools: The application uses the following external tools, all of which are open-source:
technical-tool-mongodb: <link>MongoDB</link>: a NoSQL database for storing data.
technical-tool-kafka: <link>Apache Kafka</link>: used for asynchronous communication between modules.
technical-cloning-text-1: Within the <link>GitHub project</link>, we can see the set of repositories that make up the tool.
technical-cloning-text-2: As it is developed in a modular way, we won’t need to clone all the repositories—for example, if we aren’t going to use the spells or NPC modules.

recovery-untreated-help: Untreated injury (no treatment or a failed one): the recovery roll gets the worst healing modifier. The injury still improves over time, and whatever penalty remains at the end becomes permanent.
recovery-untreated-rolled: Recovery without care: when it ends, the remaining penalty becomes permanent. Make the permanent injury roll to settle how much stays.
recovery-already-rolled: The recovery roll for the latest treatment is done. Treat the injury again to make another one.
recovery-multiplier-help: Race recovery multiplier x{{value}} (with talents): it multiplies the healing time.
permanent-check-required: Doubles on the recovery roll: roll again for permanent injury.
healing-log-rest: Rest {{hours}} h, {{days}} days: hits {{before}} → {{after}}, injuries -{{counter}} days
cauterize-heat-critical: Cauterizing inflicts a {{severity}} Heat critical: resolve it on the patient.
delete-injury-confirmation: Delete this injury? Its penalty and bleeding stop counting.
finish-at-risk-help: These characters still bleed or are dying: they are considered dead unless they are healed before finishing. Choose the fate of each one.
finish-no-characters: There are no characters in this game (NPCs are left out).
finish-tactical-game-help: Finishing closes the game: it becomes read-only and its outcome can then be applied to the strategic characters. The last round's upkeep is not run.
medical-default-difficulty: Leave the difficulty empty to use the procedure's: {{value}}.
outcome-applied-at: Applied to the strategic model on {{date}}.
outcome-applied-to-strategic: Outcome applied to the strategic model
outcome-apply-failed-n_one: {{count}} character could not be applied: retry
outcome-apply-failed-n_other: {{count}} characters could not be applied: retry
outcome-not-applied-help: The outcome has not reached the strategic characters yet: apply it to update their hits, injuries and conditions.
stabilize-no-rounds-gained: The dying actor gains no rounds.
tactical-game-finished-read-only: The game is finished: it is read-only.
hp-log-empty: No hit point changes in this round
effect-dying-help: The character is dying: they need immediate care.
effect-unconscious-help: The character is unconscious and cannot act.
effect-permanent-unconscious-help: Unconscious until healed: they do not recover by themselves.
effect-stunned-help: Stunned: a penalty to their actions while it lasts.
effect-surprised-help: Surprised: they have not been able to react yet.
effect-bleeding-help: Loses these hit points every round until the wound is treated.
health-injuries-help: Active injuries and their total penalty. Details on the character sheet.
item-condition-broken-detail: The item is broken and cannot be used until it is repaired.
item-condition-damaged-detail: Breakage damage: the penalty applies to every use of the item until it is repaired.
breakage-temporary: Temporary damage: it does not last after the game
attack-item-broken: The item of the attack is broken
err-breakage-strength-required: The item has no strength: enter it for the check
err-breakage-item-not-found: The item is not one of the actor
err-attack-item-broken: The item of the attack is broken
cauterize-heat-help: Optional: the dice of the extra hits and of the heat critical. Left empty, the server rolls the hits and leaves the critical as an alert.
cauterize-heat-critical-alert: The heat critical is waiting as an alert of the patient.
cauterize-unusual-event: Unmodified 66: the patient catches fire. The game master decides what happens.
err-injury-type-required-treatment: The treatment difficulty depends on the injury type: set the type first, or a difficulty by hand.
fear-rr-effect-help: The roll leaves no effect by itself. Apply it here, or run a fear check on the group from the round header.
fear-rr-bonus-sheet: Leave the bonus empty to use the one of the sheet: {{value}}.
fear-rr-bonus-required: This actor has no RR in its sheet: type its fear RR bonus.
group-check-fear-help: Every actor of the group makes a fear RR against the fright level. A failure leaves a fear effect, the worst one kept.
group-check-morale-help: The leader rolls Leadership to have an order obeyed, with the average fear RR of the followers.
group-check-rally-help: The leader rolls Leadership to calm the frightened followers: a success lowers or removes their fear.
group-default-help: Pick factions or actors. With none, the group is the faction of the leader.
leader-fear-help: Optional: a recognized leader adds its Leadership ranks to the fear RR of the others.
leader-roll-help: Required: the leader makes the roll and is not one of the followers.
group-check-roll-help: Leave the roll empty and the server rolls it.
member-rolls: Rolls and bonuses of each actor (optional)
member-rolls-missing-bonus_one: {{count}} actor without a fear RR bonus is left out
member-rolls-missing-bonus_other: {{count}} actors without a fear RR bonus are left out
err-group-required: Choose the group or its leader
err-intimidation-ranks-required: Type the Intimidation ranks of the NPC
leader-summary: Leader: {{ranks}} Leadership ranks, {{bonus}} to the fear RR of the followers
morale-outcome-needs-clarification: They hesitate and need it explained
morale-modifier-warning_one: Later morale rolls {{value}} for {{count}} day (apply it by hand).
morale-modifier-warning_other: Later morale rolls {{value}} for {{count}} days (apply it by hand).
unusual-misunderstands-order: Unusual event: the order is misunderstood.
unusual-leader-fired-up: Unusual event: the leader is fired up ({{bonus}} to its fear RR, {{hits}} hits). Apply it by hand.
fear-effects-help: Fear effects are kept in the actor rounds. Routed and broken actors cannot attack; the rest of their consequences are up to the game master.
maneuver-target-help: Target actor: its roll and skill bonus give the passive total.
maneuver-target-trading: The target bargains with its own Trading.
maneuver-target-awareness: The target resists with its Social Awareness.
trading-price-help: Result {{percent}}%: the deal closes at {{value}}% of the asked price.
err-action-fear: The actor is too afraid to attack
err-resistance-bonus-required: The actor has no RR bonus: type it
err-psychology-tables-missing: The psychology tables are not imported in core
err-maneuver-passive-roll-required: The target actor needs its roll
err-maneuver-target-not-found: The target actor is not in this round
err-maneuver-passive-bonus-required: Type the skill bonus of the target
err-group-actor-not-found: An actor of the group is not in this round
err-leader-not-found: The leader is not in this round
err-intimidator-not-found: The intimidating actor is not in this round
err-morale-no-followers: The leader has no followers in the group
err-rally-nobody-afraid: Nobody in the group is afraid
err-group-invalid-roll: A roll of the group is not valid
transfer-gold-to-character: Move gold from the faction to the character
transfer-gold-to-faction: Move gold from the character to the faction
price-quote-unavailable: The price cannot be worked out yet
equip-no-options: No item of the character fits this slot
item-condition-unrepairable-detail: A failed repair ruined it: it can no longer be used or repaired.
item-modifier-note-jury-rigged: Makeshift fix: it breaks on the next check
cart-empty-hint: Pick items from the catalog to add them
payer-faction-hint: Spending faction gold needs the game master.
discard-item-confirm: {{name}} (× {{amount}}) will be thrown away. The ledger keeps a record of it.
trading-maneuver-hint: Roll Trading for the character; put the Trading of the merchant as a negative modifier.
craft-enhancements-hint: Bonuses the game master grants to the new item, such as +5 to attacks.
craft-no-craftsman: The faction has no characters to work as craftsmen
craft-roll-hint: A failure wastes the materials; a better result makes a sturdier item.
ledger-outcome-wasted: The work failed and the materials are lost
ledger-outcome-halved: Half of the damage was fixed
ledger-outcome-cannot-fix-broken: Not enough to fix a broken item
ledger-outcome-jury-rigged-working: Patched up: it works for now
err-holder-forbidden: You cannot manage the items or gold of this holder
err-item-gold-not-tradable: Coins cannot be sold or crafted
err-item-holder-required: The item needs a character or a faction
err-item-not-stackable: Only a stack can be split
err-item-other-game: The holders belong to different games
err-item-other-holder: The item belongs to someone else
err-item-same-holder: The item already belongs to that holder
err-item-skill-required: Choose a skill or type a bonus
err-item-type-not-found: Item type not found in the catalog
err-item-broken: A broken item cannot be equipped
import-drop-file: Or drop an exported .rmu.json file here
import-not-json: The file is not valid JSON
import-upgraded-from: The file was upgraded from format version {{version}}
export-failed: The export could not be downloaded
import-warning-missing-skill: Skills not found here (kept and marked)
import-warning-missing-trait: Traits not found here (kept and marked, without effect)
import-warning-realm-mismatch: The file comes from another realm
import-warning-app-version: Exported with another version of the application
import-warning-hp-clipped: Hit points reduced to the new maximum
import-warning-power-clipped: Power points reduced to the new maximum
import-warning-race-skill-bonus: The race here gives different skill bonuses
err-export-invalid-file: The file is not a valid export
err-export-unknown-format: The file is not an export of this application
err-export-format-too-new: The file comes from a newer version: update the application
err-export-wrong-kind: This file holds something else than expected
err-export-character-ref-required: Choose the character of the file to import
export-character-ref-required: Choose the character of the file to import
export-wrong-kind: This file holds something else than expected
missing-reference-help: It does not exist in this installation: it came with an imported character and has no effect
roll-pad-next-die-adds: Open-ended: enter the next die, it adds
roll-pad-next-die-subtracts: Open-ended: enter the next die, it subtracts
faction-without-characters: No character of this faction can take part
roster-locked-in-progress: The game has started: characters can be added but not removed
no-instant-spells: The character knows no instantaneous spells.
err-spell-not-known: The caster does not know that spell
err-actor-without-spellbook: The actor has no character sheet with spells
err-overcast-needs-preparation: The spell is above the caster level: it needs at least one preparation round
err-spell-invalid-step: The cast is not at that step
err-spell-no-resistance: The spell allows no resistance roll
err-spell-invalid-realm: The realm is not one of the spell list
err-spell-no-attack: Only a successful cast of an attack spell makes attacks
err-spell-bolt-single-target: A bolt strikes a single target
err-spell-attack-pending: The spell attack is prepared: apply it from the attack
err-action-not-spell: The action is not a spell cast
spell-result-no-effect: No effect: the power points are lost
spell-cast-success-rr: The spell is cast (SCR {{scr}}). It is not over yet: each target rolls a resistance roll (RR) and resists if it reaches {{scr}}.
spell-cast-no-effect: SCR 0: the spell has no effect and the power points are lost.
spell-cast-failure-roll: SCR {{scr}}: the spell fails. Roll on the spell failure table to see what happens to the caster.
spell-rr-help: Resistance roll of each target: open-ended d100 + its RR bonus against {{realm}}, {{levelModifier}} for the caster level ({{level}}){{spellPart}}. It resists if the total reaches the SCR, {{scr}}; otherwise it is affected.
spell-target-affected: {{name}} does not resist (RR {{total}} against {{required}}, short by {{failure}}): affected.
spell-target-willing: {{name}} is willing: affected without a roll.
spell-outcome-failure: The spell failed: apply the spell failure result to the caster.
spell-outcome-no-rr: No resistance roll was made: decide by hand which targets are affected.
spell-outcome-all-resist: Every target resisted: the spell affects no one.
spell-outcome-no-rr-needed: The spell takes no resistance roll: its effects apply as cast.
spell-effects-manual: Not applied automatically yet: the game master applies them to the affected targets.
style-ability-max-times: Already selected as many times as allowed
style-free-ranks-help: Ranks not allocated to abilities: +2 OB each, at most +10, while fighting in the style. Allocations are permanent.
fighting-style-not-found: This style is not in the catalog
fighting-style-help: Kept in the next rounds until changed.
style-equipment-not-met: Without the equipment of the style: no bonus
style-ability-reminder: Reminder: the game master applies it
weapon-tags-help: Only what the skill and the type do not tell (fighting styles)
err-not-fighting-style: The skill is not a fighting style skill
err-style-ability-not-in-style: The ability is not part of the style
err-style-ability-repeated: The ability cannot be selected again
err-style-ability-ranks: Not enough free ranks for the ability
err-style-ability-requirements: The character does not meet the requirements of the ability
err-fighting-style-not-known: The actor has no ranks in that fighting style
err-fighting-style-option: The style does not give that ability
style-critical-option-help: Abilities of the active style that change the critical. Some must be decided now; the rest can wait for the critical roll.
style-critical-effect-leg-sweep: Leg Sweep: severity lowered from {{severity}}. The foe must beat the attack roll ({{roll}}) with a Running maneuver or fall prone.
style-critical-effect-weapon-breaker: Weapon Breaker: severity lowered from {{severity}}. The foe's weapon makes a breakage check at -25.
style-critical-effect-binding-chain: Binding Chain: Grapple critical instead of {{type}}.
style-critical-effect-redirect: Redirect: severity lowered from {{severity}}. Move the foe up to {{feet}}' in a direction of your choice, no more than they moved last round.
style-critical-effect-slowing-shot: Slowing Shot: severity lowered from {{severity}}. The foe's BMR drops {{feet}}' (to half at most).
style-critical-effect-lancers-knockback: Lancer's Knockback: severity lowered from {{severity}}. The foe is knocked back {{feet}}' and needs a medium Running or Acrobatics maneuver to stay standing.
fighting-styles-help: Each style is a specialization of its skill. Ranks of the style buy its abilities at the cost shown; unallocated ranks give +2 OB each (at most +10) while fighting in the style.
style-ability-no-description: No rule text has been imported for this ability.
alert-critical-fumble: The fumble of {{attack}} gives a critical of severity {{severity}}.
alert-critical-fumble-help: Roll it by hand, of the type the fumble text says, and apply its result. Applying the alert marks it as resolved.
err-action-cannot-attack: The actor cannot attack this round
err-attack-disarmed: The actor is disarmed: only attacks with the body are allowed
err-fumble-invalid-hits: The fumble hits are out of the range of their dice
err-fumble-invalid-dice: The fumble entry has invalid dice
err-alert-not-resolvable: This alert is resolved with its roll
attack-tables-lookup-hint: Choose a table, an armor type and a roll
combat-tables-core-law-required: The whole tables need Core Law access
difficulty-guide-no-example: The book gives no example for this difficulty.
maneuver-skill-hint: Choose a skill to see its maneuver profile, its modifiers and its example difficulties.
maneuver-roll-hint: Enter the roll to see the result.
no-skill-modifiers: This skill has no catalog modifiers.
locks-mechanism-description: Has a description of the mechanism
combat-reference-modifiers-hint: They modify the OB or DB of the attack, not this roll: they are not added to the total.
